list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.3
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.3
**Release channel:** `beta`

### ✨ Added
- [DE] **Every icon button in the desktop edition lifts and turns its glyph under the pointer.** The movement existed only on the player's transport and the round glass buttons, so the app's icon buttons - the top bar, the rows' trailing actions, the dialogs' close buttons, Listen Together's approve and reject, the window controls - were the one surface where the pointer did nothing to the glyph. All 76 `IconButton` call sites in the 16 files that held them are drawn through `M3IconButton` now: the same composable underneath, with the same click target, ripple, state layers, colours and padding, whose content sits inside `LiftedGlyph` (2 dp up and -6 degrees on the 0,6 s decelerating curve, `Modifier.iconHoverLift`). One wrapper decides the movement instead of a modifier copied 76 times, and a glyph added later cannot be drawn without it; the two buttons that are not that wrapper (Listen Together's send and the Basic player's play, both `FilledIconButton`) wrap their glyph in `LiftedGlyph` themselves, with the same `enabled` their button has. The unused `androidx.compose.material3.IconButton` imports went with the rename. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin` and `:desktop:compileTestKotlin` pass, `:desktop:motionCheck` exits 0 with `icon hover: 416 px differ between rest and lifted`, and the UI preview mirrors it: a `:is(...)` rule over its icon-button classes reads 0,6 s / `cubic-bezier(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1)` on a top-bar icon, a labelled `rail-row` keeps a still glyph, and `motion_check.mjs` and `styles_check.mjs` exit 0. **Watch:** a new icon button is an `M3IconButton`, never a bare `IconButton`, and a button of another M3 family wraps its glyph in `LiftedGlyph`. **Open sub-item:** nothing here can hover a button headlessly, so the movement is verified through its rendered end state and the preview's computed style, not by moving a pointer over every one of the 78 buttons.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.11_DE-1.56.3-beta: every icon button lifts its glyph
- docs: note the square card covers in the preview

---

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.1
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.1
**Release channel:** `beta`

### ✨ Added
- [DE] **The cookies, the clover and the icons move the way the Orion-Store site moves them: a 3D tilt that follows the pointer, and a glyph that lifts and turns.** `Motion.kt` now carries the same three numbers the site's own `data-tilt` and `.rel-icon` use (`TILT_MAX_DEGREES` 4.5 degrees per axis, `TILT_PERSPECTIVE` 900, `ICON_LIFT_DP` / `ICON_TURN_DEGREES` 2 dp and -6 degrees) and the same travel times (`Modifier.pointerTilt` 0.8 s, `Modifier.iconHoverLift` 0.6 s), both on the published decelerating curve instead of a spring, so the movement leaves at once and settles slowly like the site's `power3.out`. `pointerTilt` is what a person's cookie, an artist's card, a song's row cover, a Listen Together clover, the round glass player buttons and the Apple Music transport turn with, and `iconHoverLift` is the glyph's own half of the same rule. Both read `Motion.pointerSpec`, so the Animations master switch still makes them instant and the Animation-speed setting still scales them. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin` and `:desktop:compileTestKotlin` pass, `:desktop:motionCheck` exits 0 with its new cases reading `tilt: middle 0.00, edges -4.50 / 4.50`, `tilt: 202 px differ between flat and 4.5 degrees` and `icon hover: 416 px differ between rest and lifted`; the UI preview mirrors it, with `.md-avatar` carrying `perspective(900px) rotateX(...) rotateY(...)` and `js/chrome.js` writing the two angles from the pointer's place inside the cookie, and `motion_check.mjs` driving the real pointer path reads the corner flat, 3.60 / -3.60 degrees from a point inside its outline and flat again once the pointer has left, against `matrix(0.994522, -0.104528, 0.104528, 0.994522, 0, -2)` for the lifted glyph; `styles_check.mjs` still exits 0. **Watch:** a new surface takes the movement from `Modifier.pointerTilt` and a new glyph from `Modifier.iconHoverLift`, never from a hand-rolled rotation. **Open sub-item:** the glyph movement reaches the transport and glass controls, not every `IconButton` in the app, which keeps the state layer as its only pointer feedback.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.11_DE-1.56.1-beta: pointer tilt and icon lift on hover

---

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.2
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.2
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **"Title bar only" and "Show in title bar" exist only while the window uses the native title bar, and the reader's blocks fold when the display mode changes.** Both options write into the operating system's window title, and with the custom title bar the window is undecorated and has no title of its own to write into, so the screen offered two placements that could not show anything. `PerformanceSection` reads `nativeTitleBar` from the settings file (on `settingsFileRevision()`, so the Appearance switch reaches it at once) and draws the third display-mode row and the overlay's title-bar switch only when it is true; a mode saved as "title bar only" while the native bar was on reads as the overlay once it is off and is written back (`title bar only needs the native title bar: the reader is back on the overlay`), so the stats keep a place to draw instead of disappearing with the title they were written into. The overlay card also opens and closes through `M3SettingsFold` now, like every other block that belongs to a choice, instead of appearing or vanishing in one frame when the mode changes. The UI preview mirrors both: the third row and the title-bar switch are drawn only with `state.nativeTitleBar`, a stored "title bar only" falls back to the overlay the same way, and its four blocks fold through the existing `foldRow` on the master switch and on a mode change, with the gap above a block moved to the wrapper's padding so a closed block leaves none behind. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin` passes; the preview with the native bar off lists `Overlay in main window` and `Dedicated window` and only `Movable overlay`, and with it on adds `Title bar only` and `Show in title bar`; clicking `Dedicated window` starts one fold on the overlay block and removes it, and the master switch starts one on each of the four blocks and leaves none; `motion_check.mjs` and `styles_check.mjs` exit 0. **Watch:** a placement that writes into the OS window title has to be gated on the native title bar, and a block that belongs to a choice opens through `M3SettingsFold`. **Open sub-item:** the native title bar still only changes on the restart the Appearance toggle asks for, so the two rows appear on the next launch, like the bar itself.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.11_DE-1.56.2-beta: title bar options need the native title bar
- v6.0.8.11_DE-1.56.1-beta: pointer tilt and icon lift on hover

---
This release was built automatically from commit `832d927c05e4c30a5617f11eb9bcaace9b91d1d2`.

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.0
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.56.0
**Release channel:** `beta`

### ✨ Added
- [DE] **The full player has an "Apple Music" design, and the two player designs are named for what they are: "Basic" and "Apple Music".** "Classic" and "New" said which layout was older, never what either looked like. `player_design_classic` reads "Basic" now - its drawing is untouched and the stored `classic` key still opens it, so nobody's saved choice moves - and `player_design_new` reads "Apple Music", translated in all 53 languages of the desktop table through `scripts/desktop_extra_translations_114.py`; the brand keeps its Latin spelling the way Spotify and YouTube already do, and the mini player keeps its own "Classic small" / "New" names. The Apple Music design is a screen of its own (`ApplePlayer.kt`, `AppleMusicPlayer`): the cover and every control in one column on the left, the lyrics filling the right at 26 sp with the sung line at full ink, the artwork blurred and darkened behind both, one close control in the corner, and none of the shared chrome - no header, no "Now playing" label. It reuses `PlayerThumbnail`, `ViviSlider`, `PlayerBackground(APPLE_MUSIC)` and `LyricsScreen` with its own display options instead of reimplementing them, and its times follow Apple's convention: elapsed on the left, the time still to play on the right as a negative (`-2:23`). Three things had to be added for it to be usable rather than only drawn: a scrim of its own over the backdrop, because every control here is white ink and the app's apple backdrop draws nothing at all for a track with no artwork (white text on the light surface); the load phase and the resolve/decode error, which the shared panel draws and this screen would otherwise have hidden; and `showHeader = false` on `LyricsScreen`, whose "Lyrics" title and play/pause thumbnail would have put a second transport on top of the column. Under 720 dp the lyrics are not drawn and the column is centred, because a 26 sp strip of them is three words per line. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin` passes; the new `:desktop:applePlayerRenderCheck` paints the screen headlessly at 1280x800 and 640x800 and exits 0 (mean brightness 0.07 with no artwork, 7518 ink px in the column and 8857 in the lyrics at the wide size, 0 right of the column at the narrow one); the UI preview draws the same layout when its player design is Apple Music and reads at 1440x900 as a 315 px square cover, a 1032 px lyrics column beside it, one active line of twelve, no horizontal overflow, and the picker showing "Basic" and "Apple Music"; `styles_check.mjs`, `scroll_check.mjs`, `prefs_check.mjs`, `motion_check.mjs`, `buttons_check.mjs`, `geometry_check.mjs` and `strings_gen.py` still exit 0. **Watch:** this screen draws in ink rather than in a theme role, so anything added to it must stay legible over the darkened backdrop in both themes; a design label is a `Localization_en.kt` + `desktop_extra_translations_NNN.py` change, never a hand edit of a language table. **Open sub-item:** the check has no display attached, so the screen is verified as pixels at two sizes and in the preview, not by playing a track in the window; and Basic keeps the drawing it had, only its name changed.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.11_DE-1.56.0-beta: Basic and Apple Music player designs
- docs: record the clover morph in the preview

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.55.6
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.11_DE 1.55.6
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **A cookie and the clover morph instead of staying still.** The shapes are parametric now: `CookieShapes` keeps the numbers (side count, first vertex, corner fraction, clover lobe) and `rememberPersonCookie`, `rememberArtistCookie`, `rememberCookieShape` and `rememberCloverShape` hand back a shape at one point of its morph. A hover rounds the corners of the cookie by 55 % (the 9-sided one of a person, the 4-sided one of an artist, a song's row cover and an artist's card), a selection both tightens them by 30 % and turns the polygon by half a segment, and the clover instead fills its lobes out (+0.03 hovered, +0.045 selected), because it is a union of discs and has no corner to round. The hover rides the effects spring and the selection the spatial one, both off with the `Animations` switch, and the shape is rebuilt only when the geometry moved. The corner fraction is capped where the two tangents of one side would cross, so a very round morph cannot fold the outline over itself. The UI preview morphs the person cookie on hover too: `.md-avatar` is a CSS `path()` at its 40 px box (a `url()` clipPath swaps, it cannot interpolate) with the hovered polygon beside it, both generated by `.ignore/cookie_paths.py` from the same arithmetic. **Measured:** `:desktop:motionCheck` paints the same 80 dp cookie at its three states with no scale modifier and reads three different outlines (4874 px at rest, 4824 px hovered, 4888 px selected); `motion_check.mjs` drives the real pointer and reads the avatar's `clip-path` as a rest `path()`, a different one under the pointer and the rest one again after it leaves, with `transform` at 1 / 1.08 / 1; `styles_check.mjs`, `scroll_check.mjs`, `buttons_check.mjs`, `glyph_check.mjs`, `geometry_check.mjs`, `:desktop:cookieShapesCheck` and `:desktop:compileKotlin` all exit 0. **Watch:** a shape that wants to morph must come from `rememberPersonCookie`/`rememberArtistCookie`/`rememberCloverShape`; the fixed `fourSided`/`nineSided`/`clover` values are the rest shapes and do not animate. **Open sub-item:** the clover in the preview still only grows on hover, because its box is sized inline at four different widths and a `path()` is in px.

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The class-data-sharing archive is dumped on Linux and macOS again.** `cdsArchive` copies the build JDK's launcher into the runtime image, dumps the archive with it and deletes it again; `File.copyTo` copies the bytes, not the mode, so the copy landed with the runner's umask (644) and the JVM refused to start it - `Cannot run program.../runtime/bin/java: Exec failed, error: 13 (Permission denied)` - before it printed anything. Every desktop release since the archive was added failed on all four non-Windows packaging jobs (DEB, RPM, AppImage, both macOS), which is what held 1.55.4 and 1.55.5 back. The launcher is now marked executable after the copy, for every user, and the task fails with a message naming the file if the bit cannot be set. **Measured:** `:desktop:cdsArchive` passes here (22976 KB archive, Windows path unaffected by the bit) and the failure is reproducible only where the mode matters, so the fix is verified by the next release run on Linux and macOS. **Watch:** any file copied into the runtime image and then executed needs its mode set; a shared library does not.
